steps.title: “12 payments, 0% interest”
steps.body: Almost anything can be paid in [[installments]] today: phones, fridges, even holidays. A fridge costs €1,200 in 12 payments of €100, “without interest”. Paid at once, the same shop sells it for €1,020: 15% off. Choosing the 12 payments means borrowing €1,020 and paying back €1,200. The interest is hidden in the discount you give up: [[hidden-interest]].

stat.label: yearly interest hidden in “0% interest” when cash gets 15% off

steps.prompt: Change the cash discount and the number of payments. How small must the discount be before the payments cost less than 10% a year?

goal.hint: A discount of about 5% over 12 payments.

steps.note: Simplified: the first payment is due after one month.

steps.prompt: When is “0% interest” really without interest?
options: When paying at once gets no discount at all
steps.explanation: If the cash price is the same as the total of the payments, the split is free. Any cash discount is the price of waiting.

steps.prompt: A shop gives 15% off for cash. What are you really doing if you pick 12 payments?
options: Borrowing the cash price and paying back more
steps.explanation: You get the fridge now and pay €180 more over a year. That is a loan, whatever the label says.

goal.hint: Keep 12 payments and lower the discount to 5%.
